name_zh: De Jong Gierveld 简式孤独感量表（6题）
name_en: De Jong Gierveld Short Loneliness Scale
version: English items as published by original authors in 2010 article, grouped emotional then social

license.evidence_location: Open Access / Rights and permissions explicitly CC Attribution Noncommercial; original developers publish all six English items in Measurements; no separate English-item credit exclusion identified
license.scope_note: Use English items appearing in this original-author licensed paper, not third-party Chinese/Japanese translations. Article thanks Japanese GGP for Japanese items, so those are not included. This is narrower than claiming every edition/form of the instrument universally open.
conditions: credit Jenny De Jong Gierveld and Theo Van Tilburg
state independent Chinese translation and formatting modifications
no commercial reuse without further permission

references.citation: De Jong Gierveld J, Van Tilburg T. The De Jong Gierveld short scales for emotional and social loneliness: tested on data from 7 countries in the UN generations and gender surveys. Eur J Ageing. 2010;7:121–130.
references.use: English item wording, grouped order, scoring, missing rule, rights, adult validation

references.citation: De Jong Gierveld J, Van Tilburg TG. A 6-item scale for overall, emotional, and social loneliness: confirmatory tests on survey data. Research on Aging. 2006;28:582–598.
references.use: Original development reference; not license basis for copied wording

references.citation: Statistics Netherlands (CBS). Loneliness survey – technical explanation. 2019 Social cohesion & well-being survey, n=7398.
references.use: Optional Dutch statistical bands, not clinical thresholds

order_note: 2010 authors list emotional items together then social items; this sourcepack retains that published list order. Do not claim identical order to every standalone 2006/2019 form. Retain item identity if integration adopts a source-verified alternate order.
instructions_zh: 请根据你目前的情况，判断下面每句话与你的感受是否相符。没有标准答案。
instructions_note: Project explanatory wording; source2010 does not specify a fixed past-week/month recall window, so none added.

chinese_existing_validation.citation: Leung GTY, De Jong Gierveld J, Lam LCW. Validation of the Chinese translation of the 6-item De Jong Gierveld loneliness scale in elderly Chinese. Int Psychogeriatr.2008;20:1262–1272.
chinese_existing_validation.note: Cited by original2010 authors. Existing validated Chinese text not copied; our independent working translation is not that validated version.

items.en: I experience a general sense of emptiness

items.zh: 我想念有人在身边的感觉。

items.en: There are plenty of people that I can lean on in case of trouble
items.zh: 遇到困难时，我有很多可以依靠的人。

items.en: There are many people that I can count on completely
items.zh: 有很多人是我可以完全信赖的。

items.en: There are enough people that I feel close to
items.zh: 有足够多的人让我感到亲近。

scoring.method: sum binary recodes, not a three-point Likert sum
scoring.reverse_items_note: Positive items4–6 use no=1,middle=1,yes=0. Never apply a simple 2-x transform; middle always1 on every item.
scoring.missing: 2010 source explicitly does not compute loneliness scale scores when item scores missing. Require all6 for total and corresponding3 for each subscale. No imputation.

parameters.note: 2010 original-author study establishes dimensional scores, not a universal clinical diagnosis cutoff.

parameters.population: Dutch 2019 Social cohesion & well-being survey n=7398; statistical descriptive categorization; not Chinese clinical norm
parameters.note: CBS English never/sometimes/frequently are survey reporting labels, not added recall frequencies to the item wording. Local report uses non-diagnostic descriptions. Do not transfer 11-item thresholds.

validation_context.age: 18–79 in seven-country GGS, Japan upper age69
limitations: cross-country factor loading invariance failed; do not claim all groups directly interchangeable
not a measure of how many friends one objectively has

general.title: 你想要的联结，和眼下感受到的联结
general.body: 孤独感不只取决于身边有多少人：有时缺的是一位能说心里话的人，有时缺的是遇事可以依靠的支持。这份回答帮助你分清想补充的是哪一种联结，而不是给你贴上“不合群”的标签。
general.next_step: 可以从一个小动作开始：约一位信任的人聊近况，或者试着参加一项你愿意重复去的活动。重视关系的质量，不必给自己规定朋友数量。

fewer_signals.title: 这次回答中的孤独线索较少
fewer_signals.body: 你这次较少表达出联结不足的感受。留意那些让你感到被理解、能依靠的关系，继续给它们一点时间。结果不否定偶尔的孤独，也不是社交成绩单。

some_signals.title: 有些联结需求可能还没被满足
some_signals.body: 你的回答提示，某些时刻你可能想要更多陪伴或更可靠的支持。先看看你更想要的是“有人懂我”，还是“遇事有人可依靠”，再选择一个小行动。

more_signals.title: 你可能希望得到更多陪伴与支持
more_signals.body: 这次回答里，联结不足的感受比较突出。这不是你的过错，也不意味着以后都会这样。可以从一位信任的人开始，表达一个具体需要；如果这种感受持续让你很难受，也可以寻求专业支持。

incomplete.title: 暂不判断
incomplete.body: 有题目没有填写，暂不生成总结果。你可以补充，也可以不继续。

reports.visual: 可选两张卡片：有人懂我 / 有人可依靠。用文字说明而非红绿危险等级，不把较少朋友等同孤独。
reports.band_warning: 如未启用CBS外部描述参数，只使用general及维度叙述，不自动显示三档。
